The controller CLASSES stay instantiated (compile-safe, undriven) — the drive-call surface IS the rollback switch (no boolean needed; forward-fix by re-adding one call). RR-1: legacy listener wiring removed in the SAME chunk the new path owns it (never both live). After CR4 the legacy classes are provably dead → CR-RGATE can prove it → CR-DEL deletes them.
chunks.notes: Theme C-R / CR4. AC-RR-6. dep: CR3 (every visibility/animation/pipeline axis must have a proven-attached new owner before its drive call is removed — RR-2). RISK HIGHEST (RR-1 + RR-2 — removing a drive call before its new owner is live blanks the UI / strands a feature; mid-chunk-triage armed). Files: DictateInputMethodService.java only. Classes stay instantiated (compile-safe) — separately committed for git-revert isolation; this is the render-layer 'flip' (the C5 analogue), the deletion is CR-DEL (the C7 analogue) gated on CR-RGATE.

chunks.description: GATE chunk (D12-atomic, the C6/D2-pre analogue at the render layer). Re-run the parent keystone scenarios on the RENDER path with the legacy classes still present-but-undriven: two-keyboard switch (Spec 1 §10), FGS-survival, OOM-kill view-recreate, rotation — asserting every behaviour group G2-G16 fires through the NEW owner (not the legacy controller). Strict-Mode-Logging assertion: no visibility axis double-written. Long-press/touch parity asserts (AC-RR-1/2): RECORD 2-mode, BACKSPACE accel-delete, SPACE cursor-swipe, ENTER overlay each produce the legacy effect via the new path. Robolectric binder-harness (parent DictatePipelineServiceOverlayTransitionTest pattern, R-7 tearDown discipline). GATE OUTPUT: GREEN → orchestrator proceeds to C10-C3 (CR-DEL); RED → mid-chunk-triage, NO controller deletion until resolved.
